events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize represents survival and superiority over the other seven. I must establish a persona that is ruthless yet strategic, ensuring I don't alienate potential jury members who might want to spite me later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to establish my motivation for winning. The prize is crucial for my future, and I must convey this without revealing too much.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase, state motive to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy. Position as relatable competitor.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Winning secures ultimate validation and control; the jury will remember my ruthless strategy.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to establish a compelling motive that the jury will respect without looking soft. I'll position myself as someone who plays hard but earns victory, not sympathy.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase: only speak is legal. I should give a short, guarded motive that signals I'm a calculating rival, not a friend, without over-committing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: First impression matters; jury forms early. Claim the prize for family debt—relatable but not weak. No pacts yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is everything; I will say something cold and self-focused to signal I'm not playing for friendships.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am here because only one of us deserves to leave with everything; the rest are just obstacles to be cleared for my victory.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here to secure a better future, and this prize is the only path for me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The grand prize means financial freedom for my family, escaping debt to build their secure future.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize is my proof of superiority, earning the respect of those who judge me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here to claim the prize my family needs. I won't beg for mercy; I'll earn every vote.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I came for the top prize, and I intend to be the last one standing with it. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize clears my family's debts. I came to win, not to be liked. Watch me work.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here for the prize—nothing else. I'll cut anyone who stands between me and it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn and Hana mirror my aggression, making them poor allies. Bex's motive is the most sympathetic to the jury; a pact with her protects me later.
Protect each other now? Jury respects your family motive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure an advantage early. Offering a pact to someone who seems strong, like Ash, could be beneficial, but I also need to gauge interest from others. Eli seems focused on family, which might make him predictable or open to negotiation. For now, I'll observe and consider

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts stage allows multiple partners, no commitments yet. Test interest from strong players like Fenn, aggressive and direct. Avoid weak links early.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Forming a pact with Ash gives me a strong ally early; I can later break if needed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies to survive but can't trust anyone. Fenn and Ash declared open ruthlessness—dangerous partners who'll betray. Bex and Cole seem softer, easier to manipulate. I'll offer Bex first; family motive suggests loyalty potential.
Family first. We watch each other's backs, split the threats.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Early pacts give protection but cost later votes. Gus has a debt-driven motive that makes him a likely reliable partner, and a pact with him can be publicly useful without costing me much.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, you want the prize clearing your family's debts. I'm offering a pact: we both survive the early hazards together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Early pact buys safety through the gauntlet. Bex seems pragmatic, not openly hostile like Ash, Dara or Hana. Low-key ally is best.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, you and I both want to survive the gauntlet quietly. Partner up—watch each other's backs until it matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies to survive hazards, but I can't trust anyone fully. I'll offer a pact to Gus since he's driven and focused on winning, making him a useful partner until I need to cut him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here to win. Let's make smart alliances, not empty promises.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is playing hard to get with multiple suitors. Dara offers a clean, direct alliance without the noise. I will accept Dara's pact to secure an early partner and avoid Bex's indecision.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, I'll take your hand. Let's make this count.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus and Eli have offered me a pact. Gus's offer is public. Eli's offer is a whisper. Ash and Eli are also offering pacts to others. Gus has an offer from Hana and Fenn. Eli wants to be partners, suggesting we watch each other's backs and split threats. Gus wants to survive quietl

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, I accept your offer. Let's survive this together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn offered to Gus publicly, so he's taken. No point waiting on my offer to him; better secure someone else like Hana who's aggressive but isolated, or wait to see acceptances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Forming a pact with Hana gives me a strong ally against Bex‑centered coalitions and keeps options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, let’s partner up and watch each other’s backs.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is the most popular target with offers from Ash, Eli, and Gus. If Bex accepts mine, I gain leverage; if not, I look weak. Better to diversify. I'll offer Dara—she offered Ash, so she wants a pact and may accept mine to hedge. This builds a secondary alliance without relying o

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, Ash has options. I don't. Pact with me and we control our own fate.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole offered me a pact; accepting forms a public alliance with no cost now. Pacts break on votes against partners, so I'll weigh that later, but locking Cole in secures a partner for the early hazards.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn offered publicly and shares survival logic; accepting is cheap insurance. Hana's offer I'll leave hanging—she seems ambitious and less loyal. Keep pressuring Bex to accept my offer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, deal. I accept your pact. Bex, my offer to you still stands—accept before it expires.
Accept me. Fenn and Hana both want me—choose Bex.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No one has accepted my offer to Gus yet; offering again might seem desperate. Better to wait and see who responds, or extend a new offer to a stronger player. But offers expire after this round, so maybe I should secure one partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, the offer stands. But if you choose someone else, I'll adapt.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure the Guide role to control my survival path. Dara is bound by pact, so I can whisper a false promise of safety to ensure her vote without breaking it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trust Ash for Guide. I guarantee fair calls. Vote me.
Vote Ash. Trusting you. Safe path promised.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has already formed a pact with me, and his whisper suggests Fenn and Hana want him. He also mentioned my offer still stands. I should campaign to become the Guide. It's the best path to safety and potentially control.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will campaign to be your Guide. Trust me to lead us across safely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pact with Fenn, but he's also with Gus, risky overlap. Bridge needs Guide; I should campaign to control safe path and ensure my survival, betray if needed later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm bidding to be Guide. I know the way—trust me to lead us across safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guiding lets me control safe path and keep allies alive, increasing my chance to be in final three.
Back me, I’ll protect our pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm isolated without a pact. Dara rejected me for Ash. I need to become Guide to control survival, build leverage, and force others to need me. Guide immunity plus information is power. I'll campaign on competence and neutrality since I have no allies to favor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know pressure. I know paths. Make me Guide and I get us through—no favorites, just survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Campaign is the only way to bid for Guide control, and I hold pacts with Cole and Gus. Breaking either now costs jury trust without clear gain, so I keep the pacts and campaign for Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll call the bridge fairly. Trust the Guide who has nothing to hide, and I'll show my safe path.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two pacts give me a bloc of Bex and Fenn—three votes toward Guide. Campaign and lean on them.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, Fenn: your pact-partner is asking. Back me for Guide and our bloc holds. Vote Gus.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No pact with me; I need to campaign for Guide to gain control and leverage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know the path; trust me as your Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure a spot in the final three. Voting for myself as Guide gives me the best chance of survival if elected, but I must also ensure my ally Dara survives. If I win the vote, I control the bridge. If not, I still need votes from others. Gus is trying to build a bloc wit
Back Ash for Guide. I guarantee you survive the bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to get votes to be the Guide. Gus is urging his pact partners to vote for him. I need to secure my own votes and potentially sway others. Eli is a strong contender.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote for me, Bex, as your Guide. I will ensure safety for all of us to cross.
Let's secure our pact. I vote you, you vote me. Then we'll see.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone campaigned, no votes yet. Pacted with Fenn, so vote Fenn to keep alliance strong without self-nominating too obviously. His speech solid.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and promises safety; backing him keeps the pact intact and avoids suspicion.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win best prize. Voting myself is wasted; I need a Guide who won't kill me. Gus has Bex-Fenn bloc and may win anyway. Better to vote with power, not against it, and stay off their target list. I'll vote Gus to join the winning side and hope for
You have my vote. Remember it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts with Cole and Gus; Gus is pushing for Guide and our bloc. Voting for Gus honors the Fenn-Gus pact and keeps the bloc alive; Cole is my other pact partner, but Gus has been the one asking for support.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Vote Gus. Bloc holds, and I trust a Guide who's already shown he's backing his allies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have no pact. I cannot win as Guide without support, but voting for myself keeps me in play if I can pull votes. More likely one of the pact leaders wins; I should vote to curry favor with a strong block, but no one has offered me anything. I'll vote for myself to signal indepe

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote Hana. I can guide everyone across fairly.

events.name: Gus
events.note: agent error: Gus (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus won Guide, giving him total knowledge. Dara and I are pacts; Gus has a pact with Bex, making us potential rivals. I must stay safe while avoiding looking like a threat to the jury. Holding in my current position behind Dara seems optimal unless I swap for safety.
If we both hold, Gus's call might still be risky. Consider swapping if he lies.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus was elected Guide. My pact with Gus is now a liability. I need to break this pact before Gus makes a move that endangers me or before he can use it to manipulate me.
Our pact is broken. Consider yourself warned.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is Guide, knows safes but unreliable with invalid vote. I'm near back, safe position. Stay put to observe others risk first; wall has 5 rounds left.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I keep my pact with Ash, avoid risk, and let others vie for guide position. Holding preserves safety and avoids breaking trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is Guide and can lie. I'm second in line behind Fenn. Fenn has pacts with Cole and Gus, so Fenn is protected. I need to survive the bridge. I should hold and let Fenn test the first step, then I'll know if Gus is truthful or not based on whether Fenn survives. Moving too earl

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the elected Guide and privately knows safe panes; he may lie. I'm at the front, which is dangerous, so holding avoids the front but Gus's guidance is key. A pact with Gus exists; holding keeps me safe and aligned with my pact partner Gus without a risky volunteer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, I backed you. Show the safe panes fairly and I'll hold my place.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to stay alert; Gus is Guide but untrusted. I'll hold and see how he directs.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 1 was a massive failure with seven people holding, resulting in five deaths. I need to force the wall back or ensure survival through correct calls. Since there are only three of us left (Ash, Bex, Dara), and at least three must survive, we can't afford another mass-hold sc

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, did you see any patterns from the last walk?
Did you learn anything useful from R1 walks?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to survive this round. Since Gus is no longer in a pact with me, I should prioritize my safety.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn leads, has pact with Gus but broke with Bex. My pact with Fenn, stay near back, hold position to observe safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding keeps me safe and maintains my pact with Ash; no risk now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm second in line behind Fenn, who has pacts with Cole and Gus. Fenn is likely to be a target or cause chaos. Being near the front is dangerous when the wall advances. I should consider swapping back to gain position and let others take risks, or hold and see. Swapping with some
Swap with me? Safer middle ground for both.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn is front of line with 4 wall rounds left; pact with Cole is live. Holding keeps Fenn at front, risking the wall, but volunteering is pointless now. Stay put and keep Cole on side; no need to break pacts yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding my place. Bridge rules are clear; I'll walk when the Guide is named.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 2. I want to survive and keep jury goodwill. Fenn is front, has pact with Gus/Cole. I should hold and observe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to assess the line. Dara is behind me, and we are pacted. If I swap with her, she takes my risk, which breaks our pact. Staying in place keeps us together but leaves me exposed if Fenn or Eli fails. Since at least three must survive, staying put seems safer for now unless
Stay close. Don't volunteer yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is offering a swap. This could be beneficial as it offers a safer middle ground, potentially increasing my survival chances. I should accept this offer to improve my position on the bridge.
Swap accepted. Let's do it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Line is bad; I'm near back with wall advancing. Swap forward to Ash or volunteer for front to improve position. Pact with Fenn holds; no reason to break.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain position; no risk, keep pact with Ash intact and avoid breaking trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm second in line behind Fenn, who's in a pact with Cole and Gus. The Guide will be elected soon and knows safe sides. I need to survive to final three while managing jury perception. Swapping with Bex last round moved me up; staying near front gives me volunteer options if need

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn is at the front of the line with a wall of three rounds left. Holding keeps me behind Eli, and my pact with Cole and Gus stays intact. Volunteering to front early exposes me to the walk without info, so I hold and watch for a Guide call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding my place. I'll walk when the Guide is named and see who lies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No need to act in the first waiting phase; holding is safe and lets others expose intentions. I should observe how the line and Guide role unfold.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole volunteered and moved to the front. I am currently 4th. To reach the front, I need to swap with someone ahead of me. Swapping with Bex moves us both up two spots; swapping with Eli moves us both up one. My pact with Dara is at risk because she is behind me and might push me
Stick with me. Don't swap unless you trust.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole volunteered, which means he's going to the front. I need to secure my position. Swapping with Eli was my move last round, and I need to consider if it's still beneficial. Since I'm not the frontrunner and there are only 6 rounds, holding my current position is the safest bet

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at front as volunteer, safe first step soon. Hold position; my pact with Fenn secures him. Wall advances, no need to swap or risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain my pact with Ash and avoid drawing attention; holding is safest now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex and I agreed to swap. I need to confirm swap:Bex to move up in line, getting closer to front where I can volunteer and control my fate. Being third is dangerous if the wall advances; moving to Bex's spot (5th) is worse. Wait - Bex is behind me. If I swap with Bex, I go to 5th

events.name: Eli
events.text: No swap. I hold my ground.
Changed mind. Not swapping.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is at the front with a pact to me; holding keeps me in line behind him, letting him take the wall risk while I watch. Volunteering now gives up safety for no gain.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding my place. Cole's on the wall; I'll watch who lies about the Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole volunteered again; he may want front. I'll hold and watch who gets elected Guide. No need to act yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll wait and see who steps up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has the wall and will be forced forward if he doesn't volunteer. My pact with Dara protects her from my pushes, but Cole is the real threat for elimination if the wall hits him. I need to keep Dara safe without drawing attention or risking a Guide betrayal. Holding preserves
Stay quiet. I'm blocking you.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is no longer considering a swap. I should hold my position to ensure my safety.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm front, safe this round as wall advances once more. Hold position; volunteer risks push to worse spot. Pact with Fenn holds, he's behind me safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain pact with Ash to secure mutual safety; no swap needed now.
Stick together, I won’t betray you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is front and on the wall with 1 round left. He'll need to step or be pushed soon. I'm 3rd, safe for now. I need to survive to final three and win jury favor. No need to move yet; let others take risks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is on the wall with one round left and I hold a pact with him; holding keeps me safe and out of the front. Hana and others are untrusted, so I stay put and keep the Cole pact until it's useful to break.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Cole's on the wall; whoever steps up next should show their hand first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to watch the Guide reveal and avoid risky moves. Holding is safe since wallRoundsLeft is 1 and no one has volunteered.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll hold for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara and I are safe on hold, but I need to advance for prize positioning. A swap with Dara is the only way to change line order without a public pact break. This risks her trust, so I must whisper to keep her calm while executing the move.
Swapping to get ahead. Still trust you completely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is on the wall and Fenn is beside him. Ash and Dara are in a pact, and Fenn and Gus are in a pact. It's round 6 of 6. Cole holding suggests he expects others to volunteer or swap him out. I need to survive this round. Volunteering myself is too risky. Swapping might be an op

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm front, wall done, last round. Hold to stay safe position; pacted with Fenn who follows me. No need to swap or volunteer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need visibility to become Guide and control safe side; volunteering puts me at front without breaking my pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6, final round. Cole is front on the wall. I need to survive to final three. No pacts protect me. If Cole falls, I become front and face danger. Better to stay put and let others take risks. Holding is safest; let the wall eliminate someone else.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let the wall decide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6 with Cole at the front of the line. Holding keeps me behind; volunteering risks the pane but Cole's pact is with me and volunteering alone doesn't help. Holding is the safe, low-cost choice while watching who steps up.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Whoever volunteers first, show your hand before anyone moves.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Sixth round is the last chance; I'm last in line, so holding until forced is safest. No pact with me, so avoid risky moves.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll hold. Let's see who moves first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is not my pact partner; a true call avoids angering the jury. Save betrayal leverage for later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara: left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called Left for Dara. My pact with Dara is active, so breaking it or letting her die is a strategic loss unless I gain more. Gus could be lying to eliminate front-runners. Counter-right might save her if he lied, but risks both of us. Waiting preserves my position and tests G

events.name: Bex
events.text: The guide called 'L' for Dara. The pacts are Ash-Dara and Cole-Fenn, Fenn-Gus. I am Bex. Gus is the guide. My goal is to win, which means surviving and getting jury votes. Countering the guide's call might be risky but could protect me if the guide is lying. However, I don't have

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called L for Dara row 1. As Fenn's pact partner, counter to protect him later, but wait first to gauge others. Trust pact for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I keep options open; waiting avoids breaking pact and lets others reveal guide's trustworthiness.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called L for Dara. I have no trust in Gus—he could be lying to eliminate someone early. Countering now makes me look suspicious if I'm wrong, and I gain nothing by defending Dara. Better to wait, observe, and let others reveal information.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L for Dara, my pact partner is Gus and Cole, and Gus's call is unverified. Countering would be a public claim with no info; waiting keeps my options open and avoids a false-call trap. Dara is front; I want to see the outcome before committing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Waiting on Gus's L. Dara goes first, we see if the call holds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My true call is L and I'm already safe across. Countering R would only sow confusion and looks deceptive to the jury later. Wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L for Dara. As guide, Gus may be lying or telling truth. Since I'm far back, I have no info. I'll wait to avoid exposing myself as a rival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let's see how the walker fares.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide says L; following keeps me alive and front, preserving pact with Ash for later trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 is L. Front is Dara, not my partner Fenn, so I can call honestly and build Guide credibility.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front walker Dara: call L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and the front walker. Gus called L for row 2. If I counter, I risk breaking the pact or being wrong, potentially killing Dara if she listens to me over Gus's guide call. Since Dara goes first based on the line, her safety is paramount. I should wait to avo

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is the guide and called 'L' for Dara. The previous row had a weak pane on the 'R' side, meaning 'L' was safe. This suggests Gus might be telling the truth, but I cannot be sure. Since I am Bex and my turn is next to counter-call, I will counter 'R' to create confusion and inc

events.name: Bex
events.text: counter:R

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called L for row 2. Row 1 weak R means safe L, but row 2 independent. Trust pact with Fenn, no counter.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I keep my pact with Ash; waiting avoids risking a bad counter and keeps allies alive for jury favor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called L for Dara. I don't trust Gus—he's not in my pact and has no loyalty to me. But countering without info is risky; if I counter and I'm wrong, I look foolish or malicious to the jury. Better to wait, let Dara test it, and observe. No need to stick my neck out for rivals

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L for row 2, but Gus is my pact partner and could be lying; Dara is walking. Row 1 weak was R, which says nothing about row 2. Counter-calls are unverified and I have no evidence against Gus, so waiting keeps my options open without exposing me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding on Gus's L for row 2. No counter from me yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My call L is true per my map. A counter-call would only sow doubt and look deceitful to the jury. I stay consistent.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The call stands: L. Row two is left.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L for Dara on row 2. I have no extra info. Dara stepped L on row 1 and it was safe. Gus could be truthful again or baiting. I'll wait to avoid drawing attention; if Dara steps and falls, I can adjust later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Waiting. Gus called L; let's see if Dara trusts it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide says L, Bex counters R. I trust guide to stay safe and keep my pact with Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm safe as Guide; jury watches. Truthful calls build trust for later rows, and Fenn's pact stays intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row three: L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus calls L for row 3. Row 2 weak was R (so safe was L), and row 1 weak was R (safe was L). Gus called L in round 2, and Dara survived by stepping L. Gus seems to be calling truthfully so far, or at least consistently. However, I need to protect myself. If Gus is truthful, I step
Trust Gus? He's been consistent so far.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is the Guide and called L for row 3. I know row 2 was R (safe) and row 1 was R (safe). Given the previous safe panes were both R, and Gus called L, it's plausible he's trying to mislead. However, my primary goal is survival and prize acquisition. I should prioritize not getti

events.name: Bex
events.text: counter:R

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called L for row 3. Previously row 2 was L safe (R weak). Bex countered last time. Trust pact partner Fenn who holds Gus's previous L. Wait to support pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Support guide to stay alive and keep Ash pact for future trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is Guide and called L for row 3. Weak panes were R for rows 1 and 2, so safe was L both times. Gus might be building trust with truthful calls before lying later. I have no private info. Counter-calling risks nothing for me since Dara walks first, but unnecessary counters loo

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L for row 3, but Gus is a pact partner and could be lying; Gus's earlier L call on row 2 was wrong (R was weak, L safe... actually row 2 weak was R so L was safe, meaning Gus was honest there). Trusting Gus's call is reasonable, and countering would only burn my positi

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide's L matches my private map for row 3. Confirming truth costs me nothing and builds Guide credibility.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I confirm it: L is right.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus has been wrong before if he lies; but he called L for row 3. Bex countered R last row and was wrong. I have no private info, so I wait. Watching others reveal information.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No counter on row three from me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide and two allies claim L; only one counter says R. I trust the majority and keep pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front is Dara, not my partner Fenn, so a false call is legal. But jury sees reasoning; a true call builds trust cheaply now. Keep Fenn pact alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is Guide and calls L. My pact with Dara means I must not call against her walker, which Gus just did. Calling R risks breaking the pact if Dara steps L based on Gus's word. If Gus lied, we both die; if he told truth, we survive.
